cap_confirmation: driver state reported level_cap 60. Glimmora/Swalot/Mightyena L56 (offset -2) and Camerupt L57 (offset -1), both cap + offset - 2 on Medium.
chronology_note: New party for the hideout, built only from pool-60 gates at 42 and below so every source map precedes the raid: Amoonguss 42 (Foongus), Incineroar 36 (Litten), Urshifu-Rapid 42 (Kubfu script evolution), Gardevoir 30 with Gardevoirite stone-window 14, Zapdos 30 (New Mauville sign), Swampert 36 (Mudkip line). One reachable legend. Nothing from Shoal Cave, Route 124-127, Mossdeep, the Aqua Hideout or the Safari Zone - the Magma Hideout comes after Mt Pyre and before all of those.
pre_play_strategy_checks: Toxic Debris lays Toxic Spikes for free when Glimmora is hit by a physical move
Toxic Spikes are the hideout's shared opening investment and later rooms profit
Swalot Yawns the target it cannot remove more profitably
Swalot Encores a committed setup or Protect
Mightyena is Intimidate plus a Choice Band
Camerupt is the room's damage spike

attempts.why: Longest grunt fight in my block and the one that most deserved its length. I followed the crack on turn 1 - Fake Out went at Swalot, not at Glimmora, so no free Toxic Spikes - and Spore took Glimmora out of the fight. But Glimmora still got a 116-damage Power Gem into Incineroar first, and when I finally had to hit it physically to finish it, Toxic Debris laid two full layers of Toxic Spikes, which cost me later: Urshifu came in badly poisoned. Swalot Encored Amoonguss twice, locking it into a Spore with nothing left to sleep and then into a resisted Sludge Bomb, and its Protect blocked a lethal Thunderbolt. Incineroar died to a Play Rough crit plus a Sludge Bomb. Zapdos closed it out - its Ground immunity means Camerupt's Earth Power is dead weight - and Urshifu's Surging Strikes is 4x into a Fire/Ground body, which ended the room.

strategy_checks.check: Toxic Debris lays Toxic Spikes when Glimmora is hit physically
strategy_checks.evidence: turns 2 and 3, both times Incineroar's Knock Off connected: 'Toxic spikes were scattered on the ground all around'. Two layers by the time Glimmora died, which is the badly-poisoned tier.

strategy_checks.check: The spikes are a real shared investment the player pays for later
strategy_checks.evidence: Urshifu was badly poisoned the moment it switched in on turn 8 and took poison damage immediately. The caveat is that my lead was a Grass/POISON Amoonguss, which absorbs Toxic Spikes on entry - so one common answer switches the whole hazard off for free, and I simply never got to use it because Amoonguss started the battle on the field before the spikes existed.

strategy_checks.check: Swalot Yawns the target it cannot remove more profitably
strategy_checks.evidence: Yawn selected on turns 1 and 7 at Amoonguss, the bulkiest body on my side and the one it could not break. Correct target. Turn 1's was denied by Incineroar's Fake Out flinch, which is the crack working.

strategy_checks.result: PASS, twice, and it was the best play in the room
strategy_checks.evidence: turn 2 Encore locked Amoonguss into Spore on a board where both opponents were already asleep, so Amoonguss spent two turns doing literally nothing. Turn 5 Encore locked it into Sludge Bomb, which is 0.5x into both Poison bodies. That is precisely the authored 'Encores a committed setup' idea and it cost me more tempo than any damage this room did.

Intimidate fired on each of its two entries (turns 3 and 7), and the Banded Play Rough critted Incineroar for 124. Knock Off removed the Band on turn 4, which is the correct answer and the reason it stopped mattering.

strategy_checks.check: Camerupt is the room's damage spike
strategy_checks.evidence: Heat Wave burned Amoonguss and did 124 through its Grass half on turn 7. It is also the reason Zapdos alone could not close - Fire/Ground is immune to Electric and resists Fire, so it forced me to bring in a Water body onto the Toxic Spikes. Good structural work by a 4th slot.

protect_ledger.payoff: real - blocked Zapdos's Thunderbolt at 83/230 with paralysis already on it. That was lethal; Protect bought it a full extra turn, in which it used Yawn.

protect_summary: 1 opponent Protect, with a clean lethal-denying payoff, 0 empty, no consecutive guarding. Camerupt and Glimmora both carry Protect and neither reached for it while attacking was better. Nothing to tune.
ai_defect_summary: No AI defects, and this room made the two best non-obvious plays I saw in the hideout: Encore into a board where the Encored move was already useless, and a mid-fight switch that pulled a sleeping Mightyena out for Camerupt on turn 6 and brought it back once Camerupt had a free turn. Smart Switching is doing real work here.

level_changes.why: won on attempt 1 with one faint; Glimmora is the room's memorable idea and at 176 HP it dies to two ordinary physical hits before the hazard investment can pay off
same; of the three -2 members it contributed least - one Banded crit, then it was Spored and had to be switched out

level_change_rationale: Won first try with a single faint, so this is the review-a-+1 case. I raised the two weakest members rather than Swalot, which was comfortably the best-played body on the field and does not need help, or Camerupt, which is already -1 and did exactly its job. Both changes are +1 and within the +-2 limit; no species, move, item, ability or strategy flag was touched.
rebuild_note: The level changes cannot be re-verified from this session - the run pinned work/agent-battle-build-5, which predates the edit. The main agent must rebuild before a rerun.
theme_check: Yes. This reads as a door crew softening the player up for the rest of the base, and it is the one room where the hazard actually followed me into later turns. A crystal-flower that punishes your first physical answer, a sludge bag that punishes your first committed turn, the faction dog and the faction mount - it is coherent, it is legible on the board, and Glimmora is genuinely a species the player will not have seen before.
cooler_note: Keep it; this is the best-functioning grunt room in my block. The one thing that would make the shared hazard idea land harder, and it is a whole-hideout point rather than a criticism of this team: Toxic Spikes are absorbed on entry by any grounded Poison type and ignored entirely by anything airborne, and the later Magma rooms do not punish either of those outs. If the hideout wants the door crew's investment to be felt, one of the deeper rooms should make staying airborne expensive.
